newsitem.title: USA: Mexico buys up to 36,000 T U.S. HRW wheat - trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico buys up to 36,000 T U.S. HRW wheat - trade.

text.p: Mexico overnight bought at least 27,000 to 36,000 tonnes U.S. hard red winter wheat, U.S. exporters said.
It may have also bought a shipment of U.S. soybeans.
Mexico bought about 15,000 tonnes of U.S. HRW wheat slated for November 11-30 delivery, one U.S. exporter said.
Mexico also purchased a shipment of 21,000 tonnes of U.S. HRW wheat set for December 10-20 delivery and 5,000 tonnes HRW wheat (Mid-Bridge, Laredo) for next week shipment, he said.
The 15,000 tonnes was roughly at $169.00 a tonne FOB, and another 21,000 tonnes was at about $165.50, he said.
The wheat was shipped via rail or U.S. Gulf.
A second U.S. exporter confirmed that Mexico did buy two cargoes. "One was for 15,000 tonnes and another for 21,000 tonnes. There was a customer in for trains," he said.
But another exporter said Mexico bought a smaller amount of U.S. HRW wheat and maybe 8,000 to 10,000 tonnes U.S. soybeans.
"I think they may have bought 27,000 to 30,000 total U.S. HRW wheat and at least 8,000 to 10,000 tonnes soybeans," he said. The shipment date and price for the soybeans was not available.

So far this marketing year, Mexico has bought 787,200 tonnes U.S. HRW wheat versus 332,600 tonnes during the same period a year ago and compared with total purchases in 1995/96 of 835,400 tonnes, the U.S. Department of Agriculture said.
